speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to help me understand the cause, please describe exactly where it is located, how it started, and if you have any fever or recent injuries.

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum. Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and the rapid progression of a painful, ulcerative lesion following a minor trauma (ant bite) without signs of infection, this is highly suggestive of Pyoderma Gangrenosum, a neutrophilic dermatosis often associated with underlying inflammatory conditions.
